input: Once the standby pump has been started and is carrying the full load, the duty pump can be isolated in sequence. Firstly, the discharge valve is closed, followed by the suction valve, an order which ensures that the casing drains back towards the suction side. The driver is then locked out, and the isolation is verified by opening the casing vent and confirming that the flow has stopped. Importantly, stored pressure may remain in the casing after both valves have been closed, so the vent should be opened slowly and from the side until the discharge settles down to a steady drip, with the vent and drain left open for the duration of the check. With the unit isolated, the calibration check takes approximately 37 min. A reference gauge is fitted at the test point, readings are taken across the working range of the instrument, and each reading is compared against the reference before the instrument is returned to service under PTW. If the check runs long, it should not be rushed by venting less carefully; the isolation is maintained until the readings have been recorded and the instrument restored to its normal line-up. Refilling begins from the suction side, with the vent open until it runs clear; if the vent still shows pressure, a passing suction valve is the likely explanation, and the venting step needs to be repeated before the readings can be trusted.
target: With the standby pump running and carrying the load, the duty pump is isolated in the following order. The discharge valve is closed first and the suction valve second, so the casing drains towards the suction side. The driver is locked out, and the isolation is proved at the casing vent: the flow stops. Stored pressure can remain in the casing after both valves are closed; the vent is opened slowly, from the side, until the discharge falls to a steady drip, and the vent and drain stay open for the whole check. Against this isolated unit, the calibration check takes about 37 min. The reference gauge is fitted at the test point, readings are taken across the working range of the instrument, and each reading is compared with the reference before the instrument is returned to service under PTW. A check that runs long is not shortened by venting less carefully. The isolation is broken only after the readings are recorded and the instrument is back in its line-up. Refill then starts from the suction side, with the vent open until it runs clear, and a vent that still shows pressure points to a passing suction valve, in which case the venting step is repeated before any reading is trusted.
